gaps: SEARCH BUDGET: the turn's WebSearch budget (200 calls, shared) was exhausted before this critic ran, so no new verification was possible. Contradictions were resolved by weighing sourced lenses (shelly, enclosure, faults, hmi) against memory-only lenses (metering, gear) and by engineering reasoning; each resolution carries a confidence mark. The user can continue the search in a follow-up message.

Shelly stock list (model, generation, quantity, DIN vs flush, dry vs common-L, Pro 3EM 120A vs 3CT63, presence of a 4th 'N' CT jack) is absent from /home/user/projekt_rozdzielnicy/materialy/ (both subfolders empty). Every lens depends on it: it sets output count without purchases, coil voltage (230 V AC vs 24 V DC), DIN module count (Pro = 1 or 3 modules; Plus/Gen3 flush units need DIN adapter boxes of ~2-3 modules each) and whether 1 or 2 Modbus relay nodes must be bought. The user's instruction ('use the ones we have, there are many') makes this the gating input.

No rail-by-rail layout exists. docs/02_dobor_obudowy.md sums ~110 module-equivalents (90 devices + ~20 for terminals) but nobody allocated devices to rows or checked duct volume. The metering lens adds +7-10 modules (DIN RS485 meter 4-4.5, CKF-B 1, CP-730 3, Pro EM-50 1) plus a 150x60 mm off-rail CT bar; the hybrid architecture swaps 3-4 Pro 4PM (9-12 modules) for 2 Modbus RTU Relay (D) nodes (~145x90x40 mm, ~8 modules each, LOW confidence on size). Net demand ~120-130 module-equivalents plus a ~250 mm high power zone (toroid dia 155-165 x 82-90 mm, reversing pair 100x85x95 mm, resistor bank 200x100x40 mm + 120 mm fan).

Ampere Point AC500 Smart Load Balancer: interface (RS485 Modbus vs Wi-Fi/proprietary), CT rating/window/lead length, supply and mounting are unknown (all vendor domains blocked). This sets CT-bar conductor size (6 vs 10 mm2), gland type (M25 multi-hole), whether a 4-4.5 module RS485 meter slot and an RS485 master selector are needed, and whether the external module sits within CT lead reach (>=3 m may be needed).

WB500 and P35 fault-detection capabilities (PEN-fault/N-PE monitoring, phase-sequence check, RDC-DD 6 mA, under/over-voltage thresholds and timing) are undocumented in all lenses; without them the 'expected reaction' column of the fault matrix and the demo value of F1, F3, F7, F9, F10 are speculative. IEC 61851-1 does not mandate phase-sequence checking (only Mennekes-class units react).

Toroid (F10) switching topology is unresolved and both existing proposals are flawed: docs/01 (secondary-side changeover + bypass, 'close T1 branch then open bypass') and the faults lens (bypass 'around the DUT path, not the winding' - electrically the same thing) both pass through either a momentarily shorted energised secondary (Isc ~20-30x In, B6 trip, contact welding) or a load path through an un-energised series winding (core saturation, DUT voltage collapse). Primary-side switching with a shorted-primary neutral state was analysed by no lens (see architecture recommendation).

Availability of a 2x30 V 1000 VA toroid (faults lens choice) on Allegro is unverified; Indel TST / Breve TTS standard catalogue voltages are 2x12/2x15/2x18/2x24 V, so 2x30 V may be a custom winding (2-3 weeks, ~600-950 PLN). Fallback with stock parts: 800-1000 VA 2x24 V windings in parallel = 24 V at 33-42 A (206/254 V - marginal vs 207/253 V) plus a 2x12 V 500 VA unit for 218/242 V and 194/266 V steps.

No verified part for the PE contactor: a 25-40 A contactor with an NC MAIN pole (PE closed when de-energised) - candidates Hager ESC448 (40 A 2NO+2NC), ESC428 (25 A 2NO+2NC), Schneider A9C20848/A9C20838, Eaton Z-SCH230/40-22 / 25-22, Noark Ex9CH40 22 / Ex9CH25 22, F&F ST25-22 - all from memory, unverified. Modular contactors have no mirror contacts (IEC 60947-4-1 Annex F); positively-driven feedback for the PE pole requires an industrial contactor with a mirror-contact auxiliary (e.g. Schneider LC1D + LADN block) - not covered by the gear lens.

Both internally inconsistent. safety_concerns: Switching PE is prohibited in any installation (IEC 61851-1 clause 8.4: protective conductors shall not be switched in Mode 3/4; HD 60364-5-54 clause 543.3.3: no switching device in PE). The board is legitimate only as electrical test equipment under EN 50191: label it 'stanowisko probiercze EN 50191' (not 'rozdzielnica'), key switch 'TRYB TESTOWY' enabling the fault-coil bus, E-STOP (1 NC hard-wired in the coil bus + 1 NO to the controller), red 'USTERKA AKTYWNA / PE ROZLACZONE' and green 'NORMALNY' lamps, DUT on an insulated panel, 'nie dotykac podczas testu' signage, operation by qualified persons only.

PE must be switched only in the single DUT PE conductor, by an NC MAIN pole (PE closed when the coil is de-energised; 25-40 A, 6 mm2 rated) with a positively-driven/mirror auxiliary read back by the controller, enabled only through key switch + hardware watchdog (<=60 s auto-restore). Never switch the enclosure PE bar, door bonding or the installation PE. The docs/01 design (NO contactor held energised + manual key bridge) fails on loss of control power and must be replaced.

Backstop RCD gap: during F13 (30 mA RCD bypassed) combined with F1/F3/F5/F16 a 300 mA type S guardian offers fire protection only - lethal touch currents are not interrupted. Fit a non-bypassable 30 mA Type B backstop (accept nuisance trips during leakage demos) or hard-interlock F13 against F1/F3/F5/F6/F16 and keep the DUT behind a barrier; a Type A backstop is blind to the smooth-DC leakage ladder.

Leakage ladders (6-60 mA L->PE) together with an open PE drive up to 60 mA into the DUT chassis - above the 30 mA fibrillation threshold. Interlock in HARDWARE (ladder relay coils fed through an NC aux of K_PE and through the N-PE bridge/PE-resistor relays' NC contacts), not only in firmware; the faults lens exclusive-group logic (voltage x, PE x, N x, leakage x) must be mirrored by wiring.

Over-voltage (254-270 V) and neutral-shift (267-320 V in F4 with asymmetric 1-phase loads) can destroy DUT electronics, SPD varistors and any OUTPUT-side meter: Shelly Pro 3EM / EM-50 supply range is 100-260 V, so a neutral-shift or +15 % demo may kill the stocked meter if its voltage inputs/supply hang on the manipulated output. Limit boost to +13 % (260 V) and <=30 s, neutral shift to <=5 s with a 'sacrificial DUT' flag; place SPD, control PSUs, Shelly supplies and the HMI upstream of the fault section on the clean supply; feed the Pro 3EM voltage inputs from the output only through 2 A MCB protection and accept the 260 V ceiling.

Series toroid hazards: any state with primary energised and the series winding shorted by a bypass is a hard short (Isc ~20-30x In = 600-1000 A in the secondary, ~100 A reflected in the primary -> MCB trip, contact welding); any state with primary open while load current flows in the series winding saturates the core and collapses the DUT voltage. Use primary-side switching with a shorted-primary neutral state, electrically interlocked by NC poles so 'primary energised' and 'bypass closed' can never coincide; NTC/soft-start on the primary (inrush >100 A), B6-B10 MCB; never switch the primary under load without the short/open sequence.

Burnt-contact bank: 0.5 ohm at 32 A = 512 W, 1 ohm at 32 A = 1 kW; Al-housed resistors reach 150-200 C. Mandatory: KSD301 85-90 C NC bimetal in the K_R coil circuit, DS18B20/NTC to the controller, >=600 W rated bank on a <=0.5 K/W fan-cooled heatsink, firmware limits (60 s at 16 A, <=15 s at 32 A), >=100 mm thermal segregation from Shelly/HMI/PSUs/toroid, finger guard, filtered exhaust. Thermal-camera viewing requires opening the door - define that procedure under EN 50191 rules.

Door-mounted HMI: the door will be opened under 230/400 V for visual/thermal demos. Keep the door SELV-only (HMI 5 V USB-C and RS485, 24 V DC lamps, E-STOP/key contacts in a 24 V circuit), bond the door with a flexible PE strap, fit IP2X finger-safe covers on all live terminals, busbars and the toroid/resistor connections behind the door, and segregate SELV from LV wiring (>=10 mm or sleeving) per IEC 60204-1.

Shelly relays are 16 A NO general-purpose contacts without positive guidance or published electrical life: never in a 32 A load path, never switching PE/N directly, never as a safety interlock, not for high-cycle chattering (~1e5 operations). Pro 4PM outputs share one L - all coils on one phase (L1-N) from the coil bus; configure power_limit/current_limit/voltage_limit (max 280 V) and undervoltage_limit = 0 on PM devices so their auto-protection cannot fight the demo; keep the bench network isolated with cloud off.

Fail-safe design and watchdog: every fault contactor must be fail-safe de-energised (correct wiring restored on loss of control power); send every Shelly fault command with toggle_after (30-60 s) and re-arm it from the HMI; a hardware retriggerable watchdog relay fed by an ESP32 heartbeat (one of the ~4 free GPIOs via optocoupler, independent of RS485) drops the master coil contactor on firmware hang; read back every command within 500 ms via aux contacts (Modbus DI) and Pro 3EM values before the HMI shows a state as achieved.

N-PE swap, N-PE bridge and open-N: PE conductors in the manipulated section carry up to half of 32 A (bridge without RCD) or the full return current (swap) - use 6 mm2 PE, 25-40 A contacts, single 2NO+2NC contactors for crossovers (inherent break-before-make), mechanical interlock and >=50 ms dead time on the L2/L3 reversing pair; allow swap/bridge only when an RCD is in circuit; limit open-N with neutral-shift heaters to <=5 s.

Loose-contact chattering under 16-32 A causes arcing, contact welding and stress on the EV onboard charger: use a sacrificial industrial contactor (AC-1 life 1-2e6 ops, cycle counter in firmware, pulses >=100 ms, <=30 cycles per burst with minutes of pause) or an SSR with heatsink (genuine 40 A part, derate to 20-25 A continuous or one per phase); do not advertise it as an AFDD demo (zero-cross chopping has no arc signature).

Mass and mounting: a 1000x800x300 steel enclosure is 52 kg empty and ~75-85 kg equipped (toroid 7.5 kg, resistor bank, 20+ contactors, meters) - needs 4 load-bearing anchors (M10/M12) in a solid wall and two-person handling; a mobile use case requires a wheeled frame, not a wall box.

PE touch-voltage demo (F3): only high-impedance variants (>=100 kohm from L, <=2.3 mA; or isolated 24-50 V source + >=4.7 kohm, <=10 mA); never connect L to PE directly; even 2-10 mA is perceptible - treat the DUT as live and bar touching.

RCD/overcurrent compliance of the board's own output circuits (PN-HD 60364-7-722): the EV output needs its own 30 mA Type A (or B) RCD and its own overcurrent device (C32 3P for WB500, B16 1P for P35); a Type AC device may exist only as a clearly labelled 'wrong' demo position in the selector; the SPD must sit on the clean supply side, never on the manipulated output.
questions_for_user_ranked: 1. Jakie dokladnie Shelly macie w magazynie i ile sztuk kazdego (zdjecie etykiet lub lista): Pro 4PM, Pro 3, Pro 1 / 1PM / 2 / 2PM, Pro 3EM (120A czy 3CT63? czy ma 4. gniazdo przekladnika 'N'?), Pro EM-50, EM / 3EM, Plus 1 / 1PM / 2PM, 1 Gen3, Plus Uni, Wall Display? Od tego zalezy liczba wyjsc bez dokupowania, napiecie cewek stycznikow (230 V AC vs 24 V DC), liczba modulow DIN (Pro = szyna, Plus/Gen3 = puszki-adaptery) i czy dokupujemy 1 czy 2 moduly przekaznikowe Modbus.

2. Zakres usterek do zamrozenia przed doborem obudowy: (a) czy F13 'pominiecie RCD' z selektorem typow AC/A/B zostaje (+10 modulow, RCD typu B 600-2000 zl), (b) czy pod/przepiecie F10 ma dzialac przy pelnych 32 A (toroid 1000 VA, ok. 7,5 kg) czy wystarczy przy 16 A (1-faza), (c) czy tylko na L1? To decyduje miedzy obudowa 1000x600x300 a 1000x800x300.

3. Czy WB500 i P35 uzywane na stanowisku to egzemplarze 'do zuzycia'? Przepiecie 254-270 V, przerwa N z asymetrycznym obciazeniem (267-320 V) i upływy moga uszkodzic elektronike DUT, a takze Shelly po stronie wyjscia (zasilanie Pro 3EM max 260 V). Jesli nie - ograniczamy F10b do +13 % (260 V) i wykreslamy trojfazowa F4 z grzalkami.

4. Czy podczas pokazow F1/F3/F5/F16 (brak PE, napiecie na PE, zamiana N-PE, przerwa PEN) ktokolwiek moze dotykac ladowarki, kabla lub auta, czy to pokaz 'bez dotykania' za bariera? Decyduje o RCD strazniku: 30 mA typ B (drozszy, moze wyzwalac podczas pokazow uplywu) vs 300 mA S z twardymi blokadami sprzetowymi.

5. Jak wyprowadzamy zasilanie do ladowarki: gniazdo CEE 32 A 5P na obudowie, zaciski na stale, dodatkowe gniazdo Schuko 16 A IP44 dla P35? Czy ma byc gniazdo/wtyk Type 2 (do testera AmpCheck i do wstrzykniecia 6 mA DC za ladowarka - bez tego F15 odpada)?

6. AC500 Smart Load Balancer: jak komunikuje sie z WB500 (RS485 A/B, Wi-Fi, inne), jaki prad znamionowy i srednice okna maja przekladniki, jaka dlugosc ich przewodow i gdzie fizycznie stanie modul wzgledem rozdzielnicy? Prosba o zdjecie przekladnika z etykieta i instrukcje do materialy/karty_katalogowe/ (folder jest pusty).

7. Montaz: na stale na scianie (1000x800x300 = 52 kg pusta, ok. 75-85 kg wyposazona, 4 kotwy M10/M12) czy przewozona na szkolenia/targi (wtedy stelaz na kolkach zamiast szafy wiszacej)? Pomieszczenie wewnetrzne (wystarczy IP54 z wentylatorem filtrujacym) czy tez bus/zewnatrz?

8. Ekran 7 cali w drzwiach (drzwi beda otwierane pod napieciem - proponuje na drzwiach wylacznie obwody SELV) czy w osobnej puszce obok? Czy drzwi maja byc przeszklone (brak ofert 1000x800 na Allegro, +500-2000 zl; kamera termowizyjna i tak nie 'widzi' przez szklo)? Czy jest dostep do drukarki 3D na ramke ekranu?

9. Co ma robic 'smart licznik': licznik RS485 czytany przez wallbox/DLB (Eastron SDM630 V2 / ORNO OR-WE-516, 4-4,5 modulu), licznik MID do rozliczen, czy wystarczy Shelly Pro 3EM na HMI? Czy instrukcja WB500 wymienia obslugiwane liczniki zewnetrzne? Czy stanowisko ma pracowac bez Internetu (siec wyspowa, bez chmury Shelly, wlasny router w szafie)?

10. Aparatura i zasilanie: marka aparatury DIN budzet (Noark/ETI/F&F/Chint, ok. 2000-2500 zl) czy premium (Hager/Eaton/Schneider, ok. 4000-5000 zl)? Jaki kabel zasila rozdzielnice (5x6 czy 5x10 mm2, typ, zabezpieczenie przed nia) i jaki uklad sieci w miejscu pokazow (TN-S / TN-C-S, gdzie rozdzial PEN)?
enclosure_recommendation: PRIMARY: steel wall-mounted enclosure 1000 (H) x 800 (W) x 300 (D) mm, IP66/IK10, plain steel door, galvanised full mounting plate, bottom gland plate(s) - Rittal AX 1180.000 (Allegro offer 16422788244, 1582.41 PLN; plate 745x975x2.5 mm, 52 kg, two bottom gland plates, two cam locks, RAL 7035; 1300-1605 PLN off-Allegro at e-polimet/Morele). FIT CHECK: usable rail length per row = 745 mm plate minus 2x 40-60 mm vertical ducts = 600-645 mm = 33-35 modules/row; 4 rows at 150 mm pitch = 600 mm of height = 132-140 modules vs ~120-130 module-equivalents demanded (docs/02's 110 + metering lens +7-10 + two Modbus RTU Relay (D) nodes ~16 - 3-4 Pro 4PM) -> 10-15 modules reserve. Remaining 375 mm of plate height: ~120 mm terminal + CT-bar zone above the gland plate (four straight 100-120 mm runs L1/L2/L3/N at >=40 mm pitch for AC500 CTs and Shelly clamps, WAGO 2016/2006 + PE rows, separate 'network' and 'output' N and PE blocks) and ~250 mm power zone (toroid reserve dia 170 x 90 mm on an M8 centre bolt, reversing pair 100x85x95 mm, resistor bank 200x100x40 mm + 120 mm fan next to the exhaust grille). Depth 300 mm: 70 mm modular devices + 20 mm rail/standoffs + 40 mm wire bending + 25 mm door-mounted HMI + 60 mm duct = OK; 250 mm would be marginal. THERMAL: IEC 60890 estimate dT ~14 K at 150 W for this size; steady load ~90 W needs no cabinet fan, but fit a 150x150 filter fan (ATV2200, 58 m3/h, ~203 PLN, Allegro) low on one side and a 223x223 ClimaSys filtered outlet (NSYCAG223LPF ~166 PLN) high on the opposite side for the resistor-bank exhaust, KTS 011 thermostat (22-40 PLN); rating becomes IP54 (indoor). DOOR: cut-out ~193x111 mm for the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 (or ~165x100 mm if a 181x108 mm board is chosen) on the hinge-far half, 3D-printed bezel with closed-cell foam gasket, M3 standoffs on the 3.2 mm PCB holes; five dia 22.3 mm holes (E-STOP, key switch, 3 lamps); door wiring SELV only, flexible PE bonding strap. MOUNTING: 4x M10/M12 anchors in a load-bearing wall, equipped mass ~75-85 kg, two-person lift. ALTERNATIVE 1 (same size, Polish brand, faster/cheaper shipping): Adelid OM1008030 1000x800x300 (Allegro offer 7684269351, 1649 PLN; IP66 IK09, 1.2-1.5 mm sheet, plate + gland plate, reversible door, ~48.6 kg shipping weight) - plate dimensions unpublished: confirm >=740x960 mm with the seller before ordering; thinner sheet and lower IK than Rittal. ALTERNATIVE 2 (premium / glazed-door path): Eaton CS-108/300 (111715) 1000x800x300 (Allegro offer 17130395404, 2269-2479 PLN; 3 mm plate, 2 mm door, 1.5 mm body, foamed gasket, accessory transparent door available -> IP65) - pick if the client wants a window to show contactors switching (note: LWIR thermal cameras do not see through glass/PC); the only other glazed 1000x800x300 is Legrand Atlantic 036949 (2113 PLN promo, not on Allegro). SCOPE-REDUCED FALLBACK (not an alternative at full scope): 1000x600x300 - Eaton CS-106/300 (plate 970x550x3, 44.8 kg, 809-1462 PLN at wholesalers, no Allegro offer found) or ETI GT 100-60-30 (1175-1419 PLN) - 25 modules/row = 100 modules; viable only if F13 RCD-bypass (-10 modules), 32 A buck/boost and 3-4 Pro 4PM are dropped. REJECTED: 800x600x250/300 (plate 770 mm cannot hold 4 rows + terminals + a 250 mm power zone; the enclosure lens' 'compact alternative' contradicts docs/02); plastic/polyester (1.6x higher temperature rise, no bonded metal body, 1600-3500 PLN without plate); modular 4x18/6x24 distribution boards (97-168 mm depth, IP30/40, no room for a door HMI) - usable only as an optional 'typical home board' sub-panel. Decision inputs still needed before ordering: Polish questions 1, 2, 7, 8.
architecture_recommendation: RECOMMENDATION: HYBRID - ESP32-S3 touchscreen HMI as master, RS485 Modbus relay/DI nodes for safety-relevant and timing-critical paths, the client's stocked Shelly units for metering and slow non-safety states, all above a hardwired safety layer. WHY NOT the pure options: (a) Shelly-centric needs ~18-24 outputs = 5-6 Pro 4PM/Pro 3 (15-18 DIN modules, 1700-3000 PLN if not stocked); every fault path would hang on Wi-Fi/LAN RPC with unmeasured 10-100 ms latency; Shelly inputs are mains-referenced to the device L (no cheap SELV feedback); relays are 16 A NO general-purpose without positive guidance - unacceptable alone for PE/N/phase-sequence switching; it wins only on metering (Pro 3EM) and on using existing stock. (b) ESP32 + Modbus-only is deterministic and cheap (Waveshare Modbus RTU Relay (D): 8 relays 10 A + 8 DI 5-36 V, DIN, 148.98 PLN; 3 units = 24 RO/24 DI for ~450 PLN) but gives no metering and ignores the Shelly stock the client explicitly asked to use ('tych ktore mamy ... jak pasuja to wrzuc w projekt'). (c) Hybrid uses each where it fits and degrades gracefully if the stock turns out to be flush Plus/Gen3 modules. LAYER 0 - HARDWIRED SAFETY (independent of any controller): main isolator 4P 63 A -> non-bypassable backstop RCD (30 mA Type B if people may touch the DUT, otherwise 300 mA S plus hard interlocks) -> SPD T2 on the clean side -> fault section. Coil bus (230 V L1-N, or 24 V DC via HDR-150-24 if the stock is dry-contact Shelly 1/Plus 1) switched by master contactor K_M whose coil is in series with: key switch 'TRYB TESTOWY' (NO), E-STOP (NC), hardware watchdog relay (retriggerable off-delay, heartbeat from an HMI GPIO through an optocoupler), KSD301 85 C on the resistor bank. K_PE with NC MAIN pole in the DUT PE plus mirror/aux contact; N-PE and L-N crossovers as single 2NO+2NC contactors (inherent break-before-make, verify Hager ESC428/ESC448, Eaton Z-SCH230/25-22, Noark Ex9CH25 22); L2/L3 reversing pair Chint NC1-3210 with mechanical + electrical interlock and >=50 ms dead time; leakage-ladder relays fed through NC auxiliaries of K_PE and of the N-PE bridge relay; every fault contactor de-energised = correct wiring. Shelly units, HMI and PSUs (HDR-15-5 1 module, HDR-30-24 2 modules) powered from the clean side behind their own 2-6 A MCBs - never from the manipulated output. LAYER 1 - DETERMINISTIC I/O: two Waveshare Modbus RTU Relay (D) nodes on the HMI's isolated RS485 header (LiYCY 2x0.5 + GND, 120 ohm at both ends, ~10-20 ms per transaction at 115200 so 50 ms dead times and 50-500 ms chatter patterns are reproducible; the module's flash-on/off commands help). Node A relays: K_PE, K_PEr, K_PEu, K_N, K_NPE, K_B, K_LN, K_L3. Node B relays: K_SEQa, K_SEQb, K_INT (sacrificial contactor or SSR drive), K_R, toroid primary K_boost/K_buck, 2 spares. 16 DI: aux contacts of all fault contactors, E-STOP, key, KSD301, watchdog state, F&F CKF-B (phase sequence/loss on the OUTPUT) and CP-730 (3-phase under/over-voltage on the OUTPUT) relay outputs - the HMI shows 'fault really present', not 'relay commanded'. LAYER 2 - SHELLY WHERE IT FITS: Pro 3EM (stocked 120A preferred; 3CT63 only if buying new and no add-on needed) with clamps on the OUTPUT L1/L2/L3 (+N if the unit has the 4th jack) as the 'installer's meter': EM.GetStatus at 1 Hz over HTTP or outbound WebSocket, monitor_phase_sequence on, errors[] shown on the HMI, EMData for logging; voltage inputs via 2 A MCB, respecting its 100-260 V supply limit. Pro EM-50 or EM Gen3 (if stocked, else ~300 PLN) with clamps on output N and PE to visualise return current through PE during N-PE swap/bridge (Pro 3EM gives no PE current). Pro 4PM / Pro 3 / Pro 1 / Pro 2 / 1 Gen3 (whatever is stocked; flush units in DIN adapter boxes) for non-safety slow outputs: K_RCDin/K_RCDbyp selector, leakage ladder relays (<=60 mA, well within 16 A), cabinet fan, 230 V lamps if used; toroid buck/boost group may alternatively sit on one Pro 3 with a 3-step on-device mJS script. Every Shelly command issued with toggle_after 30-60 s and re-armed by the HMI (dead-man revert); PM devices with power/voltage/undervoltage limits disabled; Plus Uni (if stocked) as a SELV bridge for 2 extra DI/2 SSR outputs; Wall Display only as a secondary read-only panel. LAYER 3 - HMI/CONTROLLER: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 (800x480, 188-229 PLN on Allegro, buy 2), ESP-IDF + LVGL 9 via esp_lcd RGB (octal PSRAM 80-120 MHz, PCLK 12-16 MHz, bounce buffer 10 lines + 64 B cache line, CONFIG_SPIRAM_XIP_FROM_PSRAM, NVS/SD writes only in IDLE); FreeRTOS tasks UI / Comms (Modbus master + Shelly HTTP/WS) / Supervisor / Logger; scenario state machine IDLE -> ARMED (preconditions: charger idle, other faults off) -> APPLYING (ordered relay steps with read-back) -> ACTIVE (timed, re-arming toggle_after) -> RESTORING (reverse, verified by DI and Pro 3EM) -> IDLE/FAULT_ERROR, with an exclusive-group interlock table (voltage / PE / N / leakage groups) mirroring the hardware interlocks; HMI on HDR-15-5 behind its own MCB upstream of the fault section. NETWORK: in-panel 5-port switch (TP-Link LS105G ~55-69 PLN) + 2.4 GHz travel router/AP (GL.iNet GL-SFT1200 ~256 PLN) with static IPs; Shelly Pro on LAN, HMI and Plus/Gen3 on Wi-Fi; Shelly outbound WebSocket (Ws.SetConfig) to the HMI for push status; isolated bench network, cloud and digest auth off; ESP32 soft-AP only as fallback (<=8 stations). F10 TOROID TOPOLOGY (replaces both earlier proposals): series winding (2x30 V paralleled = 30 V at 33 A, 1000 VA, dia ~160 x 85 mm, 7.5 kg; fallback 2x24 V 800-1000 VA paralleled = 24 V at 33-42 A plus a 2x12 V 500 VA unit for +/-12/18/36/42 V steps) permanently in L1; switching on the PRIMARY (~4.3 A) with two 2NO+2NC 25 A modular contactors: K_boost connects primary to L1-N in one polarity, K_buck in the opposite polarity, and their NC poles in series SHORT the primary when both are off (shorted primary -> series winding impedance = leakage only, ~1-1.5 V drop at 32 A, ~4 A induced in the primary, 10-20 W loss). Sequence: normal = primary shorted; fault = open the short -> close K_boost or K_buck (one break-before-make transition, ~10-20 ms, no DUT interruption, never a shorted energised secondary); exit in reverse. Optional bypass contactor across the series winding only if interlocked against K_boost/K_buck by NC auxiliaries. NTC/soft-start on the primary feed, B6-B10 MCB, L1 only (wallbox electronics and O-PEN logic are L-N based). PURCHASE RULE (client instruction): buy no Shelly for outputs; buy a Pro 3EM only if none is stocked (120A ~410-520 PLN to reuse stocked clamps), Pro EM-50/EM Gen3 only for the N/PE-current demo, 2x Modbus RTU Relay (D) (~300 PLN), F&F CKF-B (~55-85 PLN), optional CP-730 (~150-220 PLN), one DIN-mountable watchdog/off-delay relay. DECISION TREE on the stock list (question 1): >=2 Pro 4PM or Pro 3 in stock -> one Modbus node may suffice (B only) and Shelly takes all slow states; only Plus/Gen3 flush units -> mount <=4-6 of them in DIN adapters for slow states, both Modbus nodes mandatory; no Pro 3EM -> buy one; Pro 3EM present with a 4th N jack -> buy one 120 A clamp instead of an EM-50; Pro 3EM 3CT63 in stock -> plan the main contactor coil on a Modbus relay, not on the Switch Add-on (compatibility unverified).
